title: Flintbridge credits-to-prototype path discovery
next_steps: Send security one-pager and SOC2 doc
Provide benchmark script and sample dataset
action_items: Priya - attach benchmark harness and instructions by 2026-02-06
Daniel - confirm pilot success criteria and dataset access by 2026-02-09
summary: Initial discovery for Flintbridge exploring Redwood quickstart credits and path to a short pilot. Main concerns: data residency/PII, private vs hosted tradeoffs, latency vs cost for underwriting summaries, time-to-first-token objective. Agreed to a 2-week prototype pilot with provided credits and benchmark script.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-03 15:30 EST · duration 48m · attendees: Evan (Redwood), Priya (Redwood), Liam (Redwood CSM), Daniel (CTO Flintbridge), Maya (ML Eng), Oliver (Prod).

00:00 Evan: hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate the time; quick round-robin then we'll dive into what you're trying to build.
00:22 Daniel: yeah thanks, I'll be brief — we're Flintbridge, we do underwriting automation for small business loans. we're looking to add a summarization + score explainability layer, low latency for internal ops and strict controls on customer PII.
00:45 Priya: makes sense, thanks. what's your current stack for models / infra? are you prototyping on cloud infra or local?
:58 Maya: mostly prototyping on lambda + a small GPU instance. using openai for a few PoCs but want to move away from a black box for compliance reasons and cost.
01:20 Oliver: timeline is tight — we'd like something in a sandbox in 2 weeks, and a production plan in a quarter. success metric is <300ms p95 for single-shot summaries and cost under $0.003 per call ideally.
01:45 Evan: great — that TTFT goal (time-to-first-token) is something we track — for self-serve you can be making requests in under an hour; for a hardened private deployment it's longer. We'll cover credits and quickstart paths.
02:10 Priya: quick question on PII: do you need on-prem or will VPC/private with customer-managed keys be sufficient?
02:22 Daniel: VPC with KMS integration would be ideal. we have controls that prohibit data leaving the cloud region, and we need audit logs.
02:40 Liam: Redwood Private supports a VPC control plane and KMS/HSM integrations, plus audit logging. for a pilot, though, many customers start on hosted with strict retention and then move to private when they hit scale.
03:05 Maya: okay, curious about model parity — if we start hosted and later go private, will the responses change? we need consistent scoring for regulatory audit.
03:30 Priya: good point. we surface model variants and pinning; you can pin an exact version for deterministic rollout. there will be minor differences if you change quantization or hardware, but we provide eval tooling to detect regressions and rollback.
03:55 Daniel: can you share what you mean by "eval tooling"?
04:08 Priya: sure — Redwood Console has an evals section where you can run prompt suites, compare outputs across model versions, and set regression alerts. we'll share a sample harness you can run locally too.
04:30 Oliver: and credits — how do these quickstart credits work? do they expire?
04:45 Evan: we typically give starter credits for PLG trials that cover your initial prototype — enough for a couple thousand calls depending on model. they do expire in 30 days but we can extend for pilots on request.
05:05 Daniel: perfect. for our pilot we want to run a small benchmark against a sample set of 5k documents and measure latency/cost/quality. is there a standard benchmark script?
05:25 Priya: yes, we'll provide a benchmark harness, a python script that hits the Redwood API, records per-request latency, token usage, and stores outputs for later eval. it also has a continuous batching config so you can test throughput.
05:48 Maya: when you say continuous batching, is that automatic or something we configure?
06:02 Priya: the runtime does smart batching but you can tune batch window and target batch size per route. for low-latency single-shot requests, batching is minimized. for high throughput, batching reduces unit cost.
06:28 Daniel: any hard numbers for latency on hosted for a 2k context summary?
06:40 Priya: depends on model; for medium-size LLaMA-style models on our hosted fleet p95 single-token latency can be ~15-25ms, full response depends on tokens. for your single-shot summaries under 512 tokens we often see p95 <300ms on our verified profiles. but we'll run the benchmark against your exact prompts.
07:08 Oliver: what's the tradeoff between picking a quantized model for cost vs an FP16 variant for quality?
07:22 Priya: quantization reduces memory and inference cost and often has negligible quality impact for many tasks. but for tight regulatory text like explanations you may want to compare both. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles by workload.
07:45 Daniel: security questions — SSO, SAML, RBAC?
07:55 Liam: we support SAML SSO, role-based access controls, tenant isolation. for private you can manage the control plane behind your SSO too.
08:12 Maya: and data residency — we need logs retained for 7 years for audit, is that supported?
08:22 Evan: hosted logs have configurable retention; for long-term retention and audit sealing, Private with customer-managed storage is recommended. we can also stream audit logs to your SIEM.
08:40 Daniel: great. what about encryption at rest and in transit?
08:48 Liam: TLS in transit, and KMS-backed encryption at rest. for Private we can hook into your HSM.
09:00 Oliver: can you do a quick walkthrough of the quickstart flow? we want exact steps so our infra team can anticipate.
09:12 Evan: sure — self-serve flow: sign up -> create API key -> SDK quickstart (python/js) -> sample prompt templates -> run benchmark script. typical time-to-first-token for an engineer is under an hour and the Console shows per-token cost and latency.
09:36 Daniel: will the SDK show token breakdown?
09:42 Evan: yes, Console and SDK both surface token-level cost and latency.
09:50 Maya: any gotchas with proxy infra? we run requests through a company-wide proxy that mangles long-lived connections.
10:02 Priya: some customers behind aggressive proxies use our SDK with explicit connection keepalives enabled, or run the requests from a VPC connector in the same region. we'll document that.
10:20 Daniel: ok. pilot logistics — what do you need from us to kick off?
10:28 Evan: we'll need a pilot owner, a small dataset (5k docs as you said), target prompts, success criteria, and which deployment you prefer to start on (hosted quickstart vs dedicated sandbox vs private eval).
10:45 Daniel: we'd prefer to start hosted to move fast, then evaluate dedicated if throughput/cost demands it.
10:55 Priya: totally reasonable. we often do hosted -> dedicated -> private path. dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and consistent latency SLAs.
11:12 Maya: curious about canary/rollouts — we need to be able to roll back quickly if a model change causes drift.
11:25 Priya: Redwood supports rollouts with canary percent rules, automatic fallback to pinned fallback models, and A/B splits. the Console visualizes request traces so you can correlate regressions with a deploy.
11:45 Oliver: cost: do you have a way to estimate unit cost for our 5k doc run?
11:54 Evan: rough calc: based on average token usage per doc we'll estimate total tokens and show cost per 1k tokens. we'll send a spreadsheet with multiple model options and the projected spend.
12:12 Daniel: compliance: can you sign a standard DPA + data processing addendum?
12:20 Liam: yes, we have standard DPAs and enterprise agreements; for Private we can do a more bespoke agreement.
12:35 Maya: who will own the pilot support? SLA?
12:42 Liam: for pilots, our CSM and SE pair (that's us) will support you; no formal SLA for hosted trial, but dedicated pilots can include an SLA.
12:58 Evan: quick Q from my side — do you have a benchmark environment in your VPC or do you want us to run it from hosted infra?
13:10 Daniel: prefer to run from our VPC so network factors are realistic.
13:20 Priya: we can provide a temporary token and an endpoint; if you need a VPC peering or connector we'll work through infra.
13:34 Daniel: okay. any blockers we haven't covered?
13:40 Oliver: one more — data deletion requests; patterns for removing PII from logs.
13:48 Liam: you can set retention policies and issue index-based deletion; for Private you can control logs entirely. we'll include the deletion playbook in the docs pack.
14:05 Maya: sounds good. what success criteria will you use?
14:12 Evan: agree on metrics: p95 latency <300ms, acceptable quality measured by an eval suite threshold (we'll help craft), and cost per doc in target range.
14:28 Daniel: can we get an estimate for dedicated capacity pricing?
14:34 Evan: we'll send a two-tier estimate: small reserved pool for pilot vs enterprise reserved for production; both monthly commit models with burst options.
14:48 Priya: for your initial 2-week sandbox we can bump up credits and provide a sandbox key; we'll also include the benchmark harness and a short runbook.
15:05 Oliver: timeline: when can you send the docs?
15:12 Evan: I'll email the SOC2 + DPA + benchmark harness by end of day tomorrow; Priya will include the harness and example prompt templates.
15:26 Daniel: ok let's lock a pilot kickoff for next Tuesday 11am EST, does that work?
15:34 Liam: works for us.
15:38 Maya: yes.
15:42 Evan: perfect — recap of next steps: send security docs, send benchmark script, provide quickstart credits and sandbox API key, schedule pilot kickoff next Tue, customer to provide sample dataset and success criteria.
15:58 Oliver: thanks everyone, this was productive.
16:05 Speaker 2: hmm one minor note — our compliance lead wants a short tech call about KMS; can we add that to the kickoff?
16:12 Liam: yes we'll add a 30m KMS/architecture deep-dive in the kickoff slot.
16:20 Daniel: thanks all.
16:22 Evan: thanks, we'll follow up with the pack. meeting end.

Notes and artifacts referenced: quickstart guide (link shared in chat), benchmark_harness.py (to be sent), SOC2_summary.pdf (to be sent), DPA template (link), pricing spreadsheet (to be attached).
